title: One in Four Teens Not Getting Enough Exercise
paragraphs: Young people across the world are not getting enough physical activity, according to a new study, with one in four adolescents saying they are not active on any day of the week.

An international team of researchers looked at around 390 surveys of 3.2 million adolescents aged 11 to 17 in 140 countries. The researchers counted an active day as one in which a person got at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity. Sixty minutes is the World Health Organization's recommended daily amount of exercise for children and adolescents.

The researchers found that in 2025, almost 25% — around 240 million adolescents — reported no active days a week. The global average was 2.7 active days a week, and just 14% of adolescents were active every day.

Across the world, girls reported fewer active days than boys, at an average of 2.4 days compared to 3 days for boys. And while average activity for boys didn't change much as they aged, for girls there was a decline from 2.6 days at 11 years old to 2.2 days at 17.

There were also differences between regions. In Central Asia, East Asia and the Pacific, Europe and other high-income Western countries the average was around 4 active days. In contrast, regions where incomes are lower, such as the Middle East and North Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa, averaged around 2 active days.
The study authors said regional differences could be explained by the fact that wealthier countries can afford to promote physical activity more and provide public spaces for it.

In 2018, the World Health Organization set a target for 2030 of a 15% reduction in adolescents who don't get 60 minutes of activity each day. However, according to the study, no country or region is on track to meet that target.
